parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with payroll, so the concern itself holds together. The problem is that they use different data-access abstractions. PayrollService.ts reads and writes only through the repositories it is given (EmployeeRepository, TimesheetRepository). PayrollAuditService.ts instead takes PrismaService and makes raw ORM calls (prisma.payrollAudit.create / findMany). It builds audit row ids (`${Date.now()}-${subject}`) and maps rows itself rather than going through a repository. So the module has no consistent boundary: one service works with repositories and the other works with the ORM directly. This is about mixed abstraction levels inside one module, not import direction. A smaller issue: in PayrollService.ts, the code that turns a record into a Timesheet (new Timesheet(r.id, r.employeeId, r.week, r.hours, r.approved)) appears twice, in approve() and in run(), so that mapping rule lives in two places.

violations.message: Uses PrismaService and the raw ORM (payrollAudit.create/findMany) and builds persistence ids itself. Its sibling PayrollService.ts goes only through repositories (EmployeeRepository, TimesheetRepository), so the module's data-access abstraction is inconsistent.
The record-to-Timesheet mapping new Timesheet(r.id, r.employeeId, r.week, r.hours, r.approved) is written out twice, in approve() and run(), instead of living in one place.
